svg.title: Acute kidney injury decision chart: urine indices and a renal ultrasound sort it into pre-renal, post-renal or intrinsic renal injury, and the intrinsic causes into acute tubular necrosis, acute interstitial nephritis, glomerulonephritis including rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, and atheroembolic disease; each column gives clues, investigations and management, with the AEIOU indications for dialysis

svg.text: Creatinine rising fast: BEFORE the kidney, AFTER it, or the kidney ITSELF?

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: acute kidney injury (AKI) = creatinine ↑ 44 µmol/L, or > 50% over baseline, or clearance ↓ 50%

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: rule out pre- and post-renal FIRST: the easiest · glomerular filtration rate (GFR) equations are WRONG while creatinine is

svg.text: ANY cause: DIALYSIS NOW for AEIOU = Acidosis, Electrolytes (K ↑), Ingestion of drugs or ischemia, fluid Overload, Uremia
